rows: Numerous trees blown down across northern portions of the county.
A severe thunderstorm damaged a metal shed roof and a fence.
Utility poles along Highway 90 were snapped off due to high thunderstorm winds.
A severe thunderstorm downed some trees in northern Waller County.
This wind gust was measured in a severe thunderstorm at the Houston Executive Airport.
Trees were downed, mostly around the intersection of Mayer Road and FM 1488.
Golf ball size hail blew out the windows of an apartment complex. Different size hail completely covered the ground and measured six inches deep.
Quarter sized hail was reported in Hempstead.
Golf ball sized hail was reported in Hempstead.
Hen egg sized hail was reported in Waller.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees along Highway 6 in the Hempstead area.
Thunderstorm winds downed numerous trees throughout the eastern part of the county.
Trees and power lines were downed near Oak Hollow Boulevard and FM 1488.
Thunderstorm winds downed a tree along FM 1488 near Oak Hollow Blvd.
Tornado estimated by multiple social media posts to be on the ground between the Fulshear area and the Brookshire area. Briefly touched down in a field. No significant damage.

Tornado appeared to touch down at an RV and boat storage facility then cross Interstate 10. It then damaged Pepperl Fuchs facility on north side of Interstate. Tornado crossed from Fort Bend into Waller County.

Tornado touched down near Trailer World RV and Boat Storage facility then crossed Interstate 10. It did minor damage to Bucees car wash area then ripped large air conditioning units off top of Pepperl-Fuchs building. Finally in damaged awnings near Builders First building before …
There was tree and fence damage off of Murrell Road.
Trees and a few large limbs were downed.
Some quarter sized hail but mostly pea to nickel sized hail was reported off Cane Island Parkway north of US 90.
Nickel sized hail was reported near Magnolia.

There was some short path damage in the Waters Road area. There were numerous large trees uprooted and laid down in different directions ranging from due south to due east. Estimated peak winds were 90 mph.

This tornado with estimated peak winds of 90 mph had a well defined damage path. Numerous trees were uprooted with some trunks snapped. A roof was taken off a barn. There was other straight line wind damage in the area.
The wind gust was measured at the Houston Executive Airport.
Local emergency managers reported that trees were downed across the Katy area.
An AWOS site measured a strong wind gust at Houston Executive Airport.
Some trees were downed near the Bowler Road and Kyle Drive intersection.
A large metal barn was destroyed. Trailers were rolled. Metal debris was strewn 1000 yards to the southeast. Trees were felled in multiple directions ranging from south to northwest.
Trees were downed by strong winds in the Prairie View area as the derecho moved through. Damage totals include other wind damage across the county.
Social media reports indicated widespread tree damage from the derecho in the Prairie View area.
The roof of a newly build home was damaged by strong winds from the derecho.
Wind gust occurred at mesonet station 030HC 4650 near Highway 6 and SH 290.

An emergency manager reported tornado damage in a mobile home park near Noel Lane, with cars flipped over. Survey teams confirmed damage in this area, finding trees snapped, powerlines down, roofs ripped off or partially ripped off of mobile homes. Additional damage was surveyed …
A member of the public reported ping-pong size hail near Turlington elementary school.
Emergency manager reported downed trees blocking roadway at the intersection of Clark Rd. and Oakbourne Rd.
Mesonet Station 030HC 4650 HWY 6 at SH290 measured a A 64 mph wind gust.
An emergency manager reported structural damage due to a downed tree along Diemer Road in Pattison, TX.
Storm Chaser posted on social media, reporting 60 mph winds in Waller County.
